one_liner: Research framework that decomposes regexes into reordered sub-matches via a bandit-picked plan, layered on RE2/PCRE2/Boost/ICU.
what_it_does: BLARE speeds up repeated regex matching over large line-oriented corpora by splitting one regex into components and evaluating them in a non-left-to-right order chosen by a multi-armed-bandit policy, instead of matching the whole pattern in one pass through the underlying engine. It is not a regex engine itself: it wraps RE2, PCRE2, Boost.Regex, or ICU Regex and exposes free functions per backend, e.g. `BlareRE2(lines, reg_string)` returning a `(time, match_count, other)` tuple, rather than a drop-in `Regex`/`RE2` object. Callers link against one of the four `blare_<engine>` targets and call its function directly on a vector of input lines plus the regex string.
